Create a CSV file for the current filters and settings that you can import to spreadsheet programs or text editors. For example, you can create the file for selected manufacturing methods or materials. The file contains only numbers and text.

name: Finish Explore
tooltip: Exits the Explore workspace and returns to the Generative Design workspace.
paths: Generative Design > OUTCOME VIEW > Finish Explore

name: Finish Outcome View
tooltip: Return to Explore
where: Generative Design > EXPLORE > Finish Outcome View
paths: Generative Design > EXPLORE > Finish Outcome View
Generative Design > OUTCOME VIEW > Finish Outcome View

name: Obstacle Geometry View
tooltip:
Displays obstacle geometries from your study setup in the Outcome View.

Obstacle geometries display in red on the canvas and they are semi-transparent. Manipulate the outcome to see how they influenced the final shape.

name: Preserve Geometry View
tooltip:
Displays preserve geometries from your study setup in the Outcome View.

Preserve geometries display in green on the canvas. Manipulate the outcome to see how they influenced the final shape.

name: Starting Shape View
tooltip:
Displays a starting shape from your study setup in the Outcome View.

The starting shape displays in yellow on the canvas and is semi-transparent. Manipulate the outcome to see how the starting shape influenced the final shape.

name: Add Label
tooltip:
Adds a label to an outcome iteration.

Add labels to organize and group outcomes. To display the outcomes, use the Labels filters. To rename and delete labels, go to the Outcome filters pane.

name: Add to Favorites
tooltip:
Adds an outcome iteration to favorites.

Once in favorites, you can easily view and compare it with other outcomes in the Explore views. To select the iteration, click and drag along the Iterations bar at the bottom of the Outcome View.

name: 3MF Scene Export
tooltip:
Outputs the additive build to a 3D Manufacturing Format (3MF) file.

The file can be opened in other software for further build preparation before manufacturing using an additive machine. Choose whether to the include or exclude various data in the file, such as support structures and information about the machine.

name: Create Machine Build File
tooltip:
Outputs the additive build to a machine-specific file that can be run directly on a supported additive machine.

The list of available file types that you can output depends on the machine selected in the active setup.

name: Create Machine Build File
tooltip: Lets the user choose an export file type.

name: Platform Statistics
tooltip:
Displays key information on the number of arranged components, the solid volume of the components, and the build height of the tallest component.

Also calculates the arrangement density as a percentage, based on the available build volume and build height of the components. The statistics do not consider support structures or components that have lattice structures created using Volumetric Lattice.

name: Print Statistics
tooltip:
Displays key data about your print, including estimated printing time and layer count.

Gain valuable insights into your prints to help optimize your additive manufacturing process. For FFF prints, access additional details, such as, filament usage, cost estimation, and energy consumption. For MPBF prints, find out exposure time, recoating time, and recoating time per layer.

name: Simulate Additive Toolpath
tooltip:
Simulates the generated additive toolpath selected in the Browser.

Use simulation to animate each layer of the build. Various controls let you skip forwards and backwards during the simulation and alter the simulation speed. A color legend distinguishes where the additive toolpath is used for the part and for the support structures.

name: Slice Analysis
tooltip: Analyze the arrangement of bodies within the build volume. Significant variations in cross-sectional area can lead to thermal instability during printing, resulting in warping, residual stress, and distortion.

name: Print Setting Library
tooltip:
Displays the Print Setting Library where you can create, edit, copy and paste, and import and export print settings for additive machines.

A print setting is a grouping of material-specific parameters, such as layer height, that you associate with an additive machine and it defines how a part is additively manufactured. The Print Setting Library lets you copy a standard print setting to a local or cloud folder, where it can then be edited as needed.

name: Assign Body Presets
tooltip:
Assigns presets of print settings to bodies in the active setup. This means that you can have multiple bodies on a build platform that each use different print settings.

All bodies use the default body preset defined in the Print Setting Editor, unless assigned a different one.

Note: This feature requires more than one body preset in the print settings.

name: Duplicate
tooltip:
Creates copies of selected components.

You can place the copies in various ways. Place them at the same location as the original components so you can manually move them later. Alternatively, distribute them evenly along a single axis or space them out along multiple axes for efficient arrangement.

name: Fill Build Volume
tooltip:
Automatically fills the unused space in the additive machine's build volume with as many copies of the selected component as possible.

Useful when building batches of identical parts to maximize production capacity. Or when you want to include additional parts in the extra space around the main part. Options let you adjust the size of the volume as well as restrict filling to 2D to prevent stacking. The copies of the component are added to the manufacturing model.

name: Remove Components
tooltip: Removes selected components from the active setup, so setups include only those components to be additively manufactured. Removed components remain in the manufacturing model.

name: Split Supports
tooltip:
Creates mesh bodies of support structures, enabling independent repositioning and manufacturing of supports from the main part.

The mesh bodies are added to the manufacturing model. Splitting supports is useful for working with setter supports, as it allows you to print the supports separately from the main parts. This is important because setter supports often require separate processing, such as placement in a furnace for sintering.

name: Feature Construction
tooltip:
Creates an additive toolpath for building features using multi-axis deposition technologies. For example, DED (directed energy deposition).

Build complete features on a planar or non-planar base surface. The features and the base must be separate, new bodies and not a single, joined body.

name: Arrange
tooltip:
Automatically arranges selected components so that they fit inside the additive machine's build volume. Components can be locked in place as needed and any components that cannot be arranged are placed outside the build volume.

Depending on the type of additive machine selected in the setup, the arrangement can be in 2D or 3D.

name: Automatic Orientation
tooltip:
Generates a range of optimized orientations for the selected component.

Rank the importance of different criteria to influence the possible orientations. Choose from a list of proposed orientations to meet your additive manufacturing requirements. For example, an orientation that minimizes the amount of supports needed, or an orientation that reduces the overall height of the manufactured part.

name: Interference Analysis
tooltip:
Checks for interference between selected components.

If an interference is found, the interfering components are highlighted orange, and a warning message is displayed on the Interference node in the Browser.

name: Minimize Build Height
tooltip: Finds an orientation with the smallest space requirement in X, Y, and Z for the selected components, and aligns the components with their shortest axis against the vertical.

name: Move Components
tooltip:
Translates and rotates components within the build volume.

Move components as needed to meet your additive manufacturing requirements. Reposition or adjust the angle of a component to minimize the amount of supports and material needed, achieve better feature accuracy, and increase part strength in a certain direction.

name: Place on Platform
tooltip: Moves the components directly in contact with, or with a clearance to, the platform surface and ignores attached supports and components below it.

name: Sub-Nest Group
tooltip:
Creates a group of components, called a sub-nest, which can be used in larger arrangements using the Arrange command.

You can also arrange the components within a specified volume.

name: PreCheck
tooltip:
Performs a series of checks to identify whether the active Process Simulation study can be solved.

The checks include making sure that the selected print settings can be simulated and that the body is in contact with the machine's build platform, either directly, or indirectly using support structures. Optionally also lets you change the accuracy of the FEA (finite element analysis) mesh and then generate the FEA mesh to check that it is adequate before solving the study.

name: Solve
tooltip:
Solves the active Process Simulation study and opens the Results contextual environment.

The results include recoater clearance and displacement, which shows the extent to which the part warps during the additive manufacturing process. A sufficiently refined mesh is needed to make sure that the results are accurate. Keep resolving the study with a successively finer FEA (finite element analysis) mesh until convergence is achieved.

name: Study
tooltip: Creates a Process Simulation study for a single body. A Process Simulation study uses FEA (finite element analysis) to predict a part's behavior during the additive manufacturing process, such as the extent of any warpage. Multiple studies can be created in a setup.

name: View Mesh
tooltip: Opens the Results contextual environment for viewing a previously generated FEA (finite element analysis) mesh.

name: View Results
tooltip:
Opens the Results contextual environment for viewing the results from a solved Process Simulation study.

The results include displacement and recoater clearance. Displacement shows the extent to which the part warps during the additive manufacturing process. Recoater clearance helps find potential print failures caused by interference between the recoater blade and the part being manufactured.

name: New Setup from G-Code
tooltip:
Creates a setup with an additive toolpath from a GCODE file.

Simulate the additive toolpath to check it before sending the file to an FFF machine for 3D printing.

name: Bar Support
tooltip:
Generates a bar support structure at the selected faces, bodies, or components.

This type of support structure is good for transferring heat away from parts to reduce potential deformation and is ideal for parts with small overhangs. The supports form vertical rods that connect the part to the build platform and they can join to form tree-like structures. Use this structure type on its own or with another type.

name: Base Plate Support
tooltip:
Generates a support structure on the build platform that follows the outline of the selected bodies or components.

This type of support structure enables a strong connection between the build platform and other support structures used on the part. They can help improve adhesion to, and reduce wear of, the build platform. Use this structure type with another to enhance the support of a part.

name: Cluster Contour with Polyline Support
tooltip:
Generates a polyline support structure around clusters of the selected faces, bodies, or components.

A cluster is a continuous area identified as needing support, as defined by an overhang angle. The walls can be featureless or use a patterned styling. Use this structure type with another to enhance the support of a part.

name: Delete Supports
tooltip: Removes support structures from selected faces, bodies, or components. This is useful for fine-tuning the support of your model for optimal performance.

name: Down Oriented Point Bar Support
tooltip:
Generates single bar support structures at the downward-facing corners and edges of the selected bodies or components.

This type of support structure adds supports in areas that might otherwise be missed using other types, so helps ensure parts are properly supported. The supports form vertical rods that connect the part to the build platform. Use this structure type with another to enhance the support of a part.

name: Edge with Bar Support
tooltip:
Generates bar support along a downward-facing edge of the selected bodies or components.

This type of support structure adds supports in areas that might otherwise be missed using other types, so help ensure parts are properly supported. Use this structure type on its own or with another type.

name: Edge with Polyline Support
tooltip:
Generates a polyline support structure at the downward-facing edges of the selected bodies or components.

This type of support structure adds supports in areas that might otherwise be missed using other types, so help ensure parts are properly supported. The supports are straight walls and can be featureless or use a patterned styling. Use this structure type on its own or with another type.

name: Lateral Support
tooltip:
Generates a fitted soft jaw on the side of a selected body, to securely hold it in place during manufacturing processes, such as milling.

Lateral supports are useful for parts with complex geometries, or delicate thin walls, that cannot be easily held in place on a vise. Unlike other additive support structures, Lateral Supports are typically manufactured independently of the supported body. After generating the support, you can separate it from the supported body using the Split Support tool from the Additive > Modify menu.

name: Lattice Support
tooltip:
Generates a bar support structure at the selected faces, bodies, or components.

This type of support structure fills the volume under the selected areas, provides rigidity, and is ideal for parts with large overhangs. The supports form rods to create a scaffold-like structure, which can grow adaptively at the build platform. Use this structure type with another to enhance the support of a part.

name: Medial Axis with Polyline Support
tooltip:
Generates a polyline support structure along part of the medial axis of the selected faces, bodies, or components.

This type of support structure adds supports along narrow areas that might otherwise be missed using other types. The extent of the supports at the medial axis is defined by an offset to the border of the cluster, which is a continuous area identified as needing support. Use this structure type on its own or with another type.

name: Polyline Support
tooltip:
Generates rows of polyline support structures at the selected faces, bodies, or components.

This type of support structure is easier to remove after the manufacturing process is complete and is ideal for intricate parts. The supports are straight walls that form parallel to each other and can be featureless or use a patterned styling. Use this structure type on its own or with another type.

name: Setter Support
tooltip:
Generates a support structure on the build platform that follows the outline of the selected bodies or components.

This type of support structure is for holding additively manufactured parts when placed in a furnace for sintering. Sintering is a secondary process used in some types of additive manufacturing, for example, binder jetting and metal FFF, where the deposited material is solidified and strengthened through the application of heat.

name: Solid Bar Support
tooltip:
Generates a bar support structure to support the selected face, body, or component.

Bar support structures are best used for parts that have small, specific overhanging areas that require support. The bars most often start from the build platform, branch out, and support the selected areas. A layer-by-layer animation of the support can be viewed when you simulate the additive toolpath.

name: Solid Volume Support
tooltip:
Generates a large support structure to support the selected face, body, or component.

Volume support structures are best used for parts with large overhanging areas. The support mostly consists of a sparse zigzag pattern, with a denser top to improve the quality of the supported layer. A layer-by-layer animation of the support can be viewed when you simulate the additive toolpath.

name: Surround Volume by Polyline Support
tooltip:
Generates a polyline support structure around an existing volume support.

This type of support structure forms an enveloping wall that traces the contour of a volume support. The walls can be featureless or use a patterned styling. Use this structure type with a volume support to enhance the support of a part.

name: Volume Support
tooltip:
Generates a large support structure at the selected faces, bodies, or components.

This type of support structure fills the volume under the selected areas, is typically strong, and is ideal for parts with large overhangs. The supports use a series of closed, hollow columns or a patterned styling that resembles cross-hatching. Use this structure type on its own or with another type.

name: 2D Profile
tooltip: 2D profile strategy is used for cutting on waterjet, laser, and plasma cutters.

name: Automatic Naming
tooltip:
Automatically renames nests and sheets in the browser, based on a specified naming rule.

The automatic naming helps make it easier to identify nests or sheets based on their properties. The naming rule can include information on material type, thickness, and custom text.

name: Material and Packaging Presets
tooltip:
Displays the Material and Packaging Presets dialog to let you add or specify the default preset. Adding a preset adds the material and packaging used in the current document to a new preset.

If you often use the same material and packaging for your nest studies, presets become a quick way of reusing the same material and packaging across multiple documents and across your Fusion Hub.

name: Process Material Library
tooltip:
Manages the materials and packagings in your nesting study.

Add materials and packagings, adjust dimensions and other properties, and sync with providers.

name: Create Nest Study
tooltip:
Creates a nesting study so you can see and adjust the nests that will be created to help you manufacture your part.

A nesting study contains a series of suggested nests for manufacturing your object. Each nest is a set of shapes arranged on one ore more sheets of material for cutting. Each of these sheets can be a different material. Before creating a nesting study, make sure that your shapes and their materials have packaging associated with them.

name: Generate
tooltip:
Generates one or more nests or nest studies that are selected from the browser.

Used to regenerate nests or nest studies when a design change is made to any components that are included in the nest study.

In the Edit Nest or Edit Nest Study dialog, if the Automatically Calculate Nest option is deselected, you can use the Generate command to regenerate the nests or nest studies after editing them.

name: Component Sources
tooltip:
Adds and manages source files for manufacturing.

In the Component Sources dialog box that opens, click Add Sources (+) to add files for manufacturing. Once added, you can edit properties for the objects. For example, for nesting studies, you can preview flat patterns of the objects and edit quantity, priority, orientation, and so on.

name: Import Inspection Results
tooltip:
Imports a machine-generated results file containing the measurements taken by a probe on a machine tool.

Results are added as a node in the Browser and colored results are displayed in the canvas. Analysis of the deviations from the nominals determine whether the results are in or out of tolerance. Types of results that can be imported include those from Inspect Surface, Probe WCS, and Probe Geometry.

name: Inspection Report
tooltip:
Creates a report of the currently selected inspection results. The report includes the data plus a snapshot of the current image in the canvas.

In the Browser, under the Results node, select a results folder or an individual set of results. You can create reports for imported machine-generated inspection results or for recorded manual inspections.

name: Live Connection
tooltip:
Shows inspection results in real-time and tracks progress of operations as they run on a machine tool.

Live connection avoids the need for a machine operator to import a machine-generated results file. It requires an installed Machine Connector application and a connection to a machine tool. Normally, this is a physical connection using an ethernet or serial cable, but some machine tools also support a wireless network connection.

name: Align CAD to Part
tooltip:
Defines the features needed to align a CAD model to a physical part.

Measure a combination of features using a CMM. Features can include three planes or one plane and two circles. Aligning the CAD model to the part locks the three axes of translation and three axes of rotation.

name: CMM Inspection Setup
tooltip:
Creates a setup for inspection using a CMM (coordinate measuring machine), such as a portable arm.

The setup lets you choose the CMM you want to use and set the WCS (work coordinate system).

name: Manual Inspect Surface
tooltip:
Measures surfaces on a physical part and compares the results with its CAD model.

Manual surface inspection requires an installed Machine Connector application and a connection to a CMM with a touch probe. The CAD model must be aligned to the part before you can start measuring.

name: Scan Surface
tooltip:
Scans surfaces on a physical part to create a point cloud.

Project the acquired point cloud onto a CAD model to compare the results to the nominal values. Scanning surfaces requires an installed Machine Connector application and a connection to a CMM with a scanning probe. The CAD model must be aligned to the part before you can start scanning.

name: Create Manual Inspection
tooltip:
Creates a list of items you want to inspect using a manual measuring instrument, such as a caliper, micrometer, or height gauge.

Items you can measure include the diameters of holes and bosses and certain distances, such as the distance between two holes or bosses, the distance between parallel surfaces, and the distance between a surface and a hole or boss. In addition, you can include checks, such as a simple pass/fail check or a user-defined action for when you want the inspector to record their observations.

name: Record Manual Inspection
tooltip:
Lets you record the measured values, or go through checks, for items in the manual inspection selected in the Browser.

If using a connected measuring instrument that outputs text, the instrument sends the measurement data directly to Fusion. If using a simpler, more traditional instrument, you can type the measured values using the computer's keyboard. After recording the manual inspection, optionally save the results as an inspection report.

name: Create Inspection Plan
tooltip: Creates a list of inspection operations based on existing PMI objects that can be measured.

name: Inspect Surface
tooltip:
Creates a probing operation to perform surface inspection of complex, free-form parts through a user-defined probe path.

The Inspect Surface strategy requires that you manually specify inspection points on the surface of the part. By defining these inspection points, you can accurately inspect and analyze the surface deviations, helping you determine if the part is within tolerance. Additionally, it eliminates the need to move parts between the CNC machine and a separate measuring device, such as a coordinate measuring machine (CMM), helping reduce time and effort. Inspection data can be imported from a CNC machine-generated results file or imported in real-time using a live connection.

name: Live Part Alignment
tooltip:
Uses real-time surface inspection results to update the alignment of a CAD model with its physical part on a machine tool.

Similar to part alignment, live part alignment helps to reduce alignment imprecisions, ensuring operations in a setup are accurate. But, in addition, it also provides a quicker, more automated workflow by removing the need for a machine operator to import a machine-generated results file. Live part alignment requires a connection to a machine tool.

name: Part Alignment
tooltip:
Uses imported surface inspection results to update the alignment of a CAD model with its physical part on a machine tool.

Part alignment helps to reduce alignment imprecisions, ensuring operations in a setup are accurate. It is ideal for parts with complex, free-form surfaces, such as those made by casting, forging, and additive manufacturing. Available only for machine tools with milling and inspection capabilities.

name: Probe Geometry
tooltip:
Creates a probing operation to measure and verify critical features, such as holes, bosses, surfaces, walls, channels, and corners, using probing cycle (macros) on the CNC machine. It also enables the fitting and inspection of geometric features, like circles and planes, from probed points without using probing cycles.

The Probe Geometry strategy provides several benefits. When using probing macros, it enables you to update the tool wear stored in the CNC machine''s controller, compensating for tool deflection and reduced diameter, leading to improved accuracy in future machining operations. When fitting geometric features, it enables you to set point tolerances to define acceptable variations at each probe point. Additionally, you can adjust feature tolerances specific to the selected surface type, such as planar or cylindrical surfaces, ensuring precise analysis of variations in flatness, shape, position, and diameter. Inspection data can be imported from a CNC machine-generated results file or imported in real-time using a live connection.

name: Exit Live Part Alignment
tooltip: Closes the Live Part Alignment contextual environment.
where: Manufacture > Live Part Alignment > Exit Alignment
paths: Manufacture > Live Part Alignment > Exit Alignment

name: Live Connection
tooltip:
Tracks the progress of the operations as they run on a machine tool and shows inspection results in real-time.

Based on the calculated part alignment, the work coordinate system (WCS) on the machine controller gets updated for the remaining operations in the setup. Live connection requires an installed Machine Connector application and a connection to a machine tool. Normally, this is a physical connection using an ethernet or serial cable, but some machine tools also support a wireless network connection.
where: Manufacture > Live Part Alignment > Get Results
paths: Manufacture > Live Part Alignment > Get Results

name: Post For Live Alignment
tooltip:
Creates NC code for all the operations in the setup.

The NC code contains the Inspect Surface operations, whose results will be used to calculate the part alignment, and any remaining operations in the setup. Post processing requires a post processor that supports milling and inspection.

name: 2D Adaptive Roughing
tooltip:
Creates a roughing operation that uses a more optimized toolpath that avoids abrupt direction changes.

Taper angles can be defined for any walls or islands.

name: 2D Chamfer
tooltip: Machines along contours creating a chamfered surface.

name: 2D Contour
tooltip:
Creates toolpaths based on a 2D contour. Contours can be open or closed and can be on different Z-levels, but each contour is flat (2D).

You can choose multiple roughing and finishing passes and multiple depth cuts for any contour.

name: 2D Offset Roughing (Pocket)
tooltip:
Creates a roughing operation that uses toolpaths parallel to selected geometry.

The entry can be selected anywhere on the model and includes various plunge and ramp options.

name: Bore
tooltip:
Bore creates a spiraling helical cut, that stays in contact with the selected faces.

Select cylindrical or conical faces to machine. Heights and depths are detected from the selected geometry. Cylinders, cones, circular cavities and bosses can all be machined in a single operation.

name: Circular
tooltip:
Creates circular cuts at multiple heights along the selected faces, that includes a lead in/lead out move.

Select cylindrical or conical faces to machine. Heights and depths are detected from the selected geometry. Cylinders, cones, circular cavities and bosses can all be machined in a single operation.

name: Engrave
tooltip: Machines along contours with V-shaped chamfered walls.

name: Face
tooltip:
Produces quick part facing to prepare raw stock for machining.

A Face operation removes all material from top of stock to top of model.

name: Slot
tooltip:
Mills a slot by following the slot center line of the slots.

You can select one or more entry positions, which lets you specify the end of the slot in which to plunge.

name: Thread
tooltip:
Creates a spiraling helical cut, for thread milling the selected faces.

Select cylindrical or conical faces to machine. Heights and depths are detected from the selected geometry. Cylinders, cones, circular cavities and bosses can all be machined in a single operation.

name: Trace
tooltip: Machines along contours with varying Z values and with, or without, left and right side compensation.

name: 3+2 Roughing
tooltip:
Creates a 3+2 roughing strategy for removing large amounts of material using multiple tool orientations.

Use short, rigid tools to machine challenging areas like undercuts. Rotary axes are locked during cutting to handle larger cutting forces.

Generate 3- or 5-axis toolpaths. 5-axis toolpaths consist of cutting moves that use 3+2 axes and transition moves that use simultaneous 5-axis motion. You can manually specify the 3+2 orientations, or use an automatic method based on tilting values, or a combination of both.

name: 3D Adaptive Roughing
tooltip:
A roughing strategy available for clearing large quantities of material effectively. It is unique in that it guarantees a maximum tool load at all stages of the machining cycle, and makes it possible to cut deep and with the flank of the tool without risk of breakage.

The strategy first makes a series of constant Z-layers through the part, and then clears them in stages from the bottom upwards. Because it can cut so deeply, the first step down at each stage should be the effective cutting length of the tool. Then clearing of the intermediate layers proceeds into the shallower layers to maximize the efficiency of the tool use.

name: 3D Chamfer
tooltip: Creates toolpaths to machine chamfers.

name: 3D Contour
tooltip:
Creates a finishing or semi-finishing operation for steep areas, such as vertical walls.

If a slope angle is specified, for example 30 to 90 degrees, the steep areas are machined, leaving the areas with a slope below 30 degrees for appropriate strategies.

name: 3D Offset Roughing (Pocket)
tooltip:
A conventional roughing strategy for clearing large quantities of material effectively. The part is cleared layer by layer with smooth offset contours maintaining climb milling throughout the operation.

To avoid plunging, the tool ramps down along a helical path between levels. To maintain a high feedrate and reduce machining time, sharp changes of direction are avoided by smoothing the tool motion.

name: Blend
tooltip:
Blend is a finishing strategy for machining surfaces that are between two curves. Both curves must be either open or closed.

When using open curves, the tool can lead-in with smooth movements between passes. When using closed curves, the strategy can generate a continuous spiral toolpath, which can reduce cycle time and provide a better surface finish.

name: Corner
tooltip:
Creates a finishing operation to machine any remaining stock that is left over by previous tools.

Ideal for targeting areas like internal fillets or small pockets that have been unreachable by tools used in previous operations. A threshold angle determines the boundary between steep and shallow areas. Passes can run along, or across, the contour of the geometry.

name: Deburr
tooltip:
Creates a finishing strategy to deburr external corners that are sharp or rounded.

Deburring removes unwanted pieces of material, known as burrs, left by previous operations. Deburring improves the aesthetics of the part, its fit and assembly, and reduces safety hazards when handling the part.

You can generate a 3-, 4-, or 5-axis toolpath depending on your machine's capabilities. Collisions are automatically avoided using shaft and holder clearances.

name: Flat
tooltip:
Creates a finishing operation that automatically detects all the flat areas of a part that are perpendicular to the tool orientation. Machine the flats with a type of toolpath that resembles either the Offset Roughing or Parallel strategy.

Obtain better cutting conditions by optimizing the toolpath over open pockets, as well as finish any nearby walls with the side of the tool by adding a finishing pass.

name: Flow
tooltip:
A finishing strategy, which follows the isocurves of a surface, to machine parts with curved surfaces. The machining passes and points of the toolpath are evenly spaced to provide consistent cutting motion over free-form shapes.

Flow is a 3-axis strategy by default, but multi-axis mode can be enabled. In multi-axis mode, the tool machines normal to the surface. Additional lead/lag and sideways tilt can be applied to control the contact point on the tool.

name: Flow (Old)
tooltip:
A finishing strategy, which follows the isocurves of a surface, to machine parts with curved surfaces. The machining passes and points of the toolpath are evenly spaced to provide consistent cutting motion over free-form shapes.

To get a continuous toolpath from one surface to another, ensure that the underlying isocurves of the surfaces align with each other and set the passes to run in the same isometric direction.

Flow is a 3-axis strategy by default, but multi-axis mode can be enabled. In multi-axis mode, the tool machines normal to the surface. Additional lead/lag and sideways tilt can be applied to control the contact point on the tool.

name: Geodesic
tooltip:
Creates a finishing operation to machine freeform surfaces and undercuts.

Choose between a Blend type or Scallop type toolpath. Blend is useful for machining between two similar curves. Scallop is useful for machining most freeform surfaces as it creates a constant offset from a machining boundary or specified guide curves.

You can generate a 3-, 4-, or 5-axis toolpath depending on the shape of the geometry and your machine's capabilities.

name: Horizontal
tooltip:
Automatically detects all the flat areas of the part and clears them with an offsetting path. If the flat area is shelved above the surrounding areas, the cutter moves beyond the flat areas to clean the edges.

Using the optional maximum stepdown, horizontal faces can be machined in stages, making the horizontal clearing suitable for both semi-finishing and finishing.

name: Morph
tooltip: Morph is a finishing strategy for machining shallow areas between selected contours with a consistent cutting direction.

name: Morphed Spiral
tooltip:
Similar to Spiral except that this operation generates the spiral from the selected boundary as opposed to Spiral which trims the generated passes to the machining boundary. This means that Morphed Spiral can be used for additional surfaces for which Spiral is not appropriate.

This strategy generally provides a much smoother toolpath than Scallop and is very useful when machining free-form/organic surfaces.

name: Parallel
tooltip:
A widely used finishing strategy, the passes are parallel in the XY-plane and follow the surface in the Z-direction. You can choose the angle as well as the stepover in the horizontal direction. The passes can be linked in a zigzag pattern, unidirectional, or split in down or up milling sections.

Parallel finishing passes are best suited for shallow areas and can be confined to machine only up to a given contact angle.

name: Pencil
tooltip:
Creates toolpaths along internal corners and fillets with small radii, removing material that no other tool can reach.

Whether using single or multiple passes, this strategy is ideally suited for cleaning up after other finishing strategies.

name: Project
tooltip:
A finishing strategy that allows you to machine along contours with the center of the tool. The provided contours are always projected onto the surface and so do not have to be on the actual surface.

Project is commonly used for engraving text or symbols on a surface. The tool is moved into the surface by either entering an axial offset or a negative stock to leave.

name: Radial
tooltip:
Like Spiral machining, this operation also starts from a center point, providing you with the ability to machine radial parts. It also provides the option to stop short of the center of the radial passes, where they become very dense.

The center point of the detail to be machined is located automatically, or can be user-specified. This routine can also be used with tool contact angles.

name: Ramp
tooltip:
Creates a finishing operation intended for steep areas similar to the Contour strategy. However, this strategy ramps down walls rather than machines with a constant Z, as is the case for Contour.

This ensures that the tool is engaged at all times which can be important for certain materials such as ceramics.

name: Scallop
tooltip:
Creates passes at a constant distance from one another by offsetting them inwards along the surface. The passes follow sloping and vertical walls to maintain the stepover.

Although this strategy can be used to finish an entire part, it is most commonly used to machine rest areas of a work piece, following a combination of Contour and Parallel passes.

name: Spiral
tooltip:
Creates a spiral toolpath from a given center point, generating a constant contact as it machines within a given boundary. Ideally suited for use on round shallow parts using tool contact angles up to 40 degrees, in conjunction with Contour passes for the more vertical faces.

The center point of the detail to be machined is located automatically, or can be user-specified. This strategy also supports tool contact angles.

name: Steep and Shallow
tooltip:
Creates a finishing operation that machines steep areas using Contour passes and shallow areas using Parallel or Scallop passes.

A threshold angle determines the boundary between steep and shallow areas. Passes in steep areas and shallow areas can overlap a distance to achieve a better surface finish. In shallow areas, Parallel passes are side-by-side whereas Scallop passes are offset inwards.

name: Wall
tooltip:
Creates a finishing operation that automatically detects vertical or steep wall surfaces. The strategy uses smooth swarf-style toolpaths to machine along walls, improving surface quality and tool motion.

For more complex geometry, the toolpath adapts by applying optimised contour style passes to minimise toolpath fragmentation.

name: Generate
tooltip:
Regenerates operations when they are out of date to make them valid.

Changes that affect an operation can make it out of date. In the browser, select one or more operations to regenerate. Select a container, like a setup or folder, to regenerate all child operations.

name: Machining Time
tooltip:
Displays an estimate of the total machining time for the setup, NC program, or individual operation selected in the Browser.

The machining time is determined by the sum of the feed time, the rapid time, and the tool change time. These values are calculated using the feeds and speeds of the tools, the distance of the calculated toolpaths, and the rapid feed rate for the machine tool. Scaling the feed rates up or down lets you see the impact on the machining time.

name: Post Process
tooltip:
Creates machine-specific NC code for the setup, NC program, or individual operations selected in the Browser.

Post processing converts manufacturing operations into instructions that a machine can understand. The output is an NC file that you can transfer to, and then run, on a machine. Post processing requires a post processor configuration file that works with the machine.

name: Setup Sheet
tooltip:
Generates an overview of the NC program for the CNC operator. Provides tool data, stock and work piece position, and machining statistics.

The setup sheet is fully customizable.

name: Simulate
tooltip:
Simulates the movement of the tool along toolpaths, visualizes the change in stock material, and highlights collisions between tool and stock.

The simulation does not use information from the machine or post processor and is therefore less accurate. If you want a more accurate representation, ensure the setup has a simulation-ready machine selected and use Simulate with Machine.

name: Simulate with Machine
tooltip:
Simulates the movement of the machine and the tool along toolpaths, visualizes the change in stock material, and highlights collisions.

The simulation uses kinematics information from the machine and post processor to represent the movements of the machine more accurately. Machine simulation requires a setup with a simulation-ready machine selected. If the setup does not have a simulation-ready machine, the simulation does not use any information from the machine or post processor and is therefore less accurate.

name: Drill
tooltip: Provides access to a wide range of drilling, tapping and hole making operations, such as counterbores and countersinks.

name: Hole Machining
tooltip:
Create folders to group operations.

You can create separate folders for roughing, semi-finishing, and finishing operations.

name: Hole Manager
tooltip: Opens the hole manager, allowing the status of all holes in the model to be managed

name: Hole Recognition
tooltip:
Automates the drilling process by detecting cylinders in the model and creating operations.

It evaluates cylinders in any orientation to provide a list of possible operations. They depend on the hole type. Next, you can select an operation that you want to apply.

name: Export Defaults
tooltip: Exports a file with the default settings of the Manufacturing toolpath strategies. Save a variety of configurations based on the machine type or different machining disciplines.

name: Form Mill
tooltip: Form Mill allows you to create a custom shaped tool from an imported CAD drawing or a sketch.

name: Import Defaults
tooltip:
Imports default settings for all the toolpath strategies in the Manufacture workspace.

Use it to quickly reconfigure default toolpath parameters. Import a configuration based on the type of machine or machining process. Importing defaults does not affect operations in the current document.

name: Machine Library
tooltip:
Manages machine definitions, enabling you to find, create, and edit descriptions of CNC machines and additive printers.

For CNC machines, you can link a post processor and a machine model to a machine definition. Linking a post processor optimizes the generated NC code, while linking a machine model enables visualization during simulation. The Machine Builder, accessible when editing a machine definition, allows you to assign components, adjust axis directions, and verify movements by jogging axes.

name: Milling Tool Holder
tooltip:
Creates a milling tool holder from a solid body.

A 2D cross-section is extracted from the body and revolved around an axis to define the holder's 3D geometry. The holder is added to the active document in the Tool Library for use in operations and simulation. Requires one solid body in the current design that represents the holder.

name: Post Library
tooltip: Displays the Post Library where you can manage posts for your projects as well as the predefined posts

name: Reset Defaults
tooltip:
Resets all of the parameter settings in the Manufacturing toolpath strategies to their built in defaults.

Existing operations in the current document are not affected by resetting the defaults.

name: Setup Sheet Configurations
tooltip: Displays the Setup Sheet Configurator where you can create and edit setup sheet configurations to be used while viewing setup sheets

name: Stock Materials Library
tooltip:
Displays the Stock Material Library where you can create and manage stock materials.

The stock material selected in a setup groups the matching tool presets for easier selection. Populate your libraries with stock materials to match what you have on the shop floor. Stock materials have a name and a type. They can also have keywords for alternative names, and they can be associated with physical materials.

name: Task Manager
tooltip:
Enables you to control background tasks, such as toolpath generation, and stop them if needed.

View the state, progress, and elapsed time for each task. If you spot issues in the toolpath preview on the model, abort the task.

name: Template Library
tooltip: Displays the Template Library where you can manage templates for your projects

name: Tool Block
tooltip: Creates a tool block from a solid body, so you can define the key connection points, defining accurate holder geometry and connection points.

name: Tool Library
tooltip: Displays the Tool Library dialog box where you manage tools for your individual documents and operations, as well as libraries of predefined tools.

name: Turning Tool Holder
tooltip: Creates a turning tool holder from a solid body, so you can define the key connection points, defining accurate holder geometry and connection points.

name: Delete Passes
tooltip:
Deletes an area of a toolpath that is specified by a selection type.

Using Delete Passes to remove unwanted areas of a toolpath is quicker than trimming by placing points over a toolpath. This is because Delete Passes lets you select individual passes or segments.

Choose between a selection type of Passes, which are individual cutting moves between the lead and link moves, or choose a selection type of Segments, which are parts of the toolpath that make up an individual cutting move and are joined by the toolpath's points.

name: Feedrate
tooltip:
Modifies the feedrate for selected toolpath moves without recalculating the toolpath.

Use this modification to fine-tune speeds for specific passes, leads, links, or segments. This can improve surface finish, tool life, and machining efficiency in areas with high material engagement or complex geometry.

1- Selected segments

2- Selected passes

name: Leads and Links
tooltip:
Modifies all or a selection of individual leads and links without needing to recalculate the entire toolpath.

Using this modification, you can add more efficiency and safety to your toolpaths by modifying things like the clearance area type, clearance heights, and changing the type of leads and links. You can also add smaller lead or link moves in places where the toolpath was not able to initially.

name: Move Entry Positions
tooltip:
Moves the tool entry and exit positions on closed toolpath passes without needing to recalculate the toolpath.

You can move the entry positions so that the tool does not enter the part where there is heavy material engagement, such as internal corners for example. You can also stagger the entry positions to avoid dwell marks on the part. Lastly, you can move the entry positions to a place where the tool entry is visible to the operator for safer machining.

When using the command, sketch a line to intersect the closed passes at the desired new entry positions.

name: Replace Tool
tooltip:
Replaces the tool that a toolpath uses without needing to recalculate the toolpath.

Short tools tend to vibrate less than longer tools, providing a better surface finish. However, a short tool may not be suitable to machine an entire part because of possible collisions. A use case could be to trim and keep both parts of a toolpath, use the short tool on the toolpath that has the most coverage, and then use a longer tool on the other toolpath to machine the remainder.

In the Browser, select a toolpath, then use the Replace Tool modification. A dialog appears to let you replace the tool, and if required, type any notes.

name: Trim
tooltip:
Trims an area of a toolpath and then adds new, gouge-free leads and links without needing to recalculate the entire toolpath.

Trimming can improve the efficiency of your toolpaths by removing unwanted passes, giving you a reduction in machining time. It can also improve toolpath safety, for example, by removing passes to avoid clamping fixtures that are not modeled.

Perform a trim using a polygon, plane, or boundary and specify whether to keep certain areas of the toolpath, or to split the toolpath.

name: Advanced Swarf
tooltip:
A multi-axis strategy that machines straight-sided walls with the side of the tool. You can machine walls accurately with a large stepover, which reduces the number of passes required and reduces cycle time.

A common use case is to machine parts with pockets or bosses that have a positive, negative, or variable draft angle, for example aerospace parts.

You can generate a 3-, 4-, or 5-axis swarf toolpath depending on the shape of the geometry and your machine's capabilities.

name: Multi-Axis Contour
tooltip: A multi-axis strategy for machining with the tip of the tool along a given contact curve. By default the tool is normal to the surface, but lead/lag and sideways tilt can be applied, when desired, to control the contact point on the tool. The strategy allows center, left, and right compensation.

name: Multi-Axis Finishing
tooltip:
Creates a finishing strategy to machine geometry such as curved floors or walls of pockets.

This strategy supports circle segment tools, which are sometimes referred to as barrel tools, to machine complex parts such as molds. The curved cutting geometry in circle segment tools allows for larger stepovers, resulting in faster cycle times.

When programming, you can target either walls or floors. The strategy automatically uses a suitable contact point on the tool, but you can manually specify a contact point with a minimum and maximum range to reach smaller corners or have smoother rotary motion.

name: Multi-Axis Roughing
tooltip:
Creates a multi-axis roughing operation to rough out areas such as pockets with floors that are not entirely flat.

The strategy offsets the specified floor surfaces to create the toolpath. This removes the stock effectively by not leaving behind any steps on the floor surface. You can also use ceiling surfaces to change the shape of the toolpath.

For multiple pockets, floor surfaces need to be connected tangentially. You can use construction geometry to create a surface that spans all the pockets you need to clear.

name: Rotary Contour
tooltip:
A multi-axis finishing strategy that lets you machine steep walls on parts that are machined most efficiently when using the 4th machine axis.

You can also machine parts that have spiralled walls to a high-quality surface finish.

name: Rotary Offset Roughing (Pocket)
tooltip:
A multi-axis roughing strategy that lets you clear large quantities of material on parts that are machined most efficiently when using the 4th machine axis.

Improve machining time by using a variable stepdown to remove the maximum amount of stock for each stepdown. Improve cutting conditions by offsetting the tool to cut with the leading edge of the tool instead of its center point.

name: Rotary Parallel
tooltip:
A multi-axis machining strategy that lets you machine along and around a rotating axis. Rotary Parallel can be used for parts that are machined most efficiently when utilizing the 4th machine axis.

For more control, you have the choice of either a continuous spiral, circular or line style toolpath. The circular and line style toolpaths can be contained by specifying angular limits around the rotary axis.

name: Swarf
tooltip: A multi-axis strategy for machining with the side of the tool. This strategy supports both machining from contours only and from surfaces. When machining from contours only, you are required to manually synchronize the contours. Swarf supports several different cutting modes that control how to machine down the sides.

name: Selection Bar
tooltip: Use window, freeform, or paint selection, invert selections, apply filters, and hide or show geometry to refine your selection.

name: Create Manufacturing Model
tooltip:
Creates a model for use in the Manufacture workspace that you can edit without affecting the original model in the Design workspace.

After creating a manufacturing model, in the browser, double-click the manufacturing model to access a contextual environment where you can use common design tools.

A common use case is to create a manufacturing model for an additive workflow that resembles the final part, referred to as a near-net-shape (NNS). You can use this part as the stock for another setup and then use a subtractive workflow to machine any final features, like holes, to complete the part.

name: Create NC Program
tooltip:
Group toolpaths from multiple setups into a new combined NC Program.

Reduce tool changes on setups with multiple fixtures and improve efficiency by completing all similar operations.

Create multiple NC Program groups for different postprocessing situations.

name: Insert Manufacturing Data
tooltip:
Adds all the setups and operations from designs you've inserted into the current document. When added, you can adjust, suppress, simulate, and post process the setups and operations.

If you haven't inserted any designs that include manufacturing data, or if the setups and operations are already added, this option has no effect.

name: Manual NC
tooltip:
Adds operations to the NC output that are machine dependent.

These functions are used to turn on or off a machine accessory, like a parts catcher, chip conveyor or program stops. No visual cue is displayed in the canvas. These functions are passed directly to the Post Processor for output to the NC program.

Post Processor customization may be required.

name: New Folder
tooltip:
Create folders to group operations.

You can create separate folders for roughing, semi-finishing, and finishing operations.

name: New Pattern
tooltip:
Duplicates a single toolpath instance that can be used for multiple instances in the same part.

Patterns can be mirrored as well as generated in rectangular or circular configurations.

name: New Setup
tooltip:
Setup is an important first step in starting your manufacturing process. These selections will help you define the working model, stock size, fixtures and set the Work Coordinate System (WCS) zero.

Available work environments

- Milling, 2 thru 5 Axis

- Turning & Mill/Turn

- Waterjet, Plasma or Laser Cutting

- 3D Printing/Additive

name: New Setup Group
tooltip: TODO

name: Probe WCS
tooltip:
Creates a probing operation to locate stock and features and update the work coordinate system (WCS) using probing cycles (macros) on the CNC machine.

The Probe WCS strategy enables you to locate stock and identify features such as holes, bosses, surfaces, walls, channels, and corners. By performing measurements against specified tolerances, this strategy helps identify variations and enables actions based on the inspection results. It also provides the capability to update the WCS Offset defined in the setup, compensating for any deviations and improving the accuracy of future machining operations. Inspection data can be imported from a CNC machine-generated results file or imported in real-time using a live connection.

name: Edit Alignment
tooltip:
Specifies the type of transformation that can be used to calculate the part alignment.

The type of transformation must be supported by the machine tool and the post processor. Currently, transformation for live part alignment is restricted to 3-axis translation only.
paths: Manufacture > Live Part Alignment > Edit Alignment

name: Exit Part Alignment
tooltip: Closes the Part Alignment contextual environment.

name: Import Inspection Results
tooltip:
Imports a machine-generated results file and calculates the part alignment.

The results show whether the surface is in tolerance after the part alignment has been applied. The results are added as a node in the Browser and colored confetti, pins, or cylinders are displayed in the canvas.

name: Show Part Alignment Information
tooltip:
Shows the transformation needed for the part alignment and how it changes the deviation of the inspection results.

Click a result in the graph to highlight it in the canvas.
paths: Manufacture > Live Part Alignment > Get Results

name: Show Results
tooltip:
Shows the detailed inspection results after the part alignment has been applied.

The results show whether the part is in or out of tolerance and by how much. Switch to showing the results without the part alignment applied to see the difference in the deviation.
paths: Manufacture > Live Part Alignment > Get Results

name: Inspect Surface
tooltip:
Creates an operation for inspecting the surface of a part using a probe.

The results from inspection are used to calculate the part alignment and update the work coordinate system (WCS) on the machine controller for the remaining operations in the setup. Ensure that there is a good distribution of points over the part.
paths: Manufacture > Live Part Alignment > Inspect Surface

name: Post For Alignment
tooltip:
Creates NC code for the Inspect Surface operations in the setup, whose results will be used to calculate the part alignment.

Post processing requires a post processor that supports milling and inspection.
where: Manufacture > Part Alignment > Post for Alignment
paths: Manufacture > Part Alignment > Post for Alignment

name: Post with Alignment
tooltip:
Creates NC code for the remaining operations in the setup with the part alignment applied.

The work coordinate system (WCS) on the machine controller gets updated for the remaining operations. The Inspect Surface operations, whose results were used to calculate the part alignment, are not included. Post processing requires a post processor that supports milling and inspection.
where: Manufacture > Part Alignment > Post with Alignment
paths: Manufacture > Part Alignment > Post with Alignment

name: Export Color 3MF
tooltip:
Creates a 3D Manufacturing Format (3MF) file which contains a color-coded displacement representation of the warped part.

The stage of the warped part that is exported is when the part has not had supports removed and is still attached to the build platform. Support structures are not included in this exported 3MF file.

name: Export Compensated STL
tooltip:
Creates an STL file of the inverse-warped part. This compensates for the displacement predicted by the solved Process Simulation study.

Based on the simulated results, the original shape of the part is automatically modified to correct for the warpage. When additively manufacturing the compensated part, the part then warps to the originally desired shape.

name: Export Warped STL
tooltip:
Creates an STL file of the warped part as predicted by the solved Process Simulation study.

The STL file can be used to validate the Process Simulation study. For example, by comparing the predicted displacement with scans of the real displacement.

name: Export Compensated
tooltip:
Creates a mesh body that automatically compensates for the displacement predicted in the solved Process Simulation study, and closes the Results contextual environment

The mesh body is added to a new manufacturing model, which you can then modify as needed. When additively manufacturing a compensated part, the part warps to the originally desired shape.

name: Open Results Folder
tooltip: Opens the folder location where the input files, log files, and result files for the Process Simulation study are stored.

name: Toggle Element Edges
tooltip: Switches between showing, and not showing, the edges of the elements in the FEA (finite element analysis) mesh.

name: Toggle Min/Max Probes
tooltip:
Switches between showing, and not showing, the locations for the minimum and maximum values for the currently selected result type.

The results include displacement and recoater clearance.

name: Finish Results
tooltip: Exits the Results contextual environment.

name: Machine
tooltip:
Shows or hides the machine tool in the canvas during simulation.

Show the machine to visually verify its movements. When showing the machine, use the options in the Simulate dialog to show or hide the machine's base or make the machine transparent.

name: Stock
tooltip:
Shows or hides the stock in the canvas during simulation.

Stock represents the workpiece from which a part is manufactured. When showing the stock, use the Colorization options in the Simulate dialog to differentiate stock depending on material, operation type, or tool usage, or to show if there is excess or gouged stock.

name: Toolpaths
tooltip:
Shows or hides the toolpaths in the canvas during simulation.

Toolpaths consist of link moves, lead moves, cutting moves, and points. Lead moves are the entry to, and exit from, cutting moves, while link moves occur between cutting moves. Points show where each move starts and ends. When showing the toolpaths, use the options in the Simulate dialog to show or hide different move types and points.

name: Exit Simulation
tooltip: Closes the Simulation contextual environment.

name: Issues
tooltip:
Lists any errors or warnings found during the verification process, such as collisions.

Clicking a row in the list of errors and warnings jumps to the issue in the timeline and updates the canvas. Any process issues that affect the simulation are listed separately. Settings let you choose whether to stop the simulation playback when an error or warning is encountered.

name: NC Code
tooltip:
Shows the NC code for the simulated NC program, setup, or individual operations, and highlights the specific line of code currently being simulated.

Seeing the NC code can be useful when analyzing errors or warnings found during the verification process. Clicking a line of NC code jumps to that point in the simulation.

name: Stock to Model
tooltip:
Displays the distance between the model's surface and the stock.

The distance is displayed when you place the pointer over the stock in the canvas during simulation. As you move the pointer, the distance is updated. A positive distance means excess stock. A negative distance means gouged stock.

name: Simulate Faster (GPU)
tooltip:
Switches between using the computer processor (CPU) and the graphics processor (GPU) for simulating manufacturing operations.

When selected, simulation uses the GPU. When deselected, simulation uses the CPU. Using the GPU enables faster processing but depends on the quality of the graphics processor. Faster simulation using the GPU does not currently support all features and cannot be used for DED (directed energy deposition) or turning operations.

name: Flute
tooltip:
Shows the tool's flute in the canvas during simulation.

A flute is the cutting edge of a tool.

name: Hide Tool
tooltip: Hides the tool's flute, shaft, and holder in the canvas during simulation.

name: Holder
tooltip:
Shows the tool's holder, shaft, and flute in the canvas during simulation.

A flute is the cutting edge of a tool. A shaft is the upper section of the tool and fits into a holder.

name: Shaft
tooltip:
Shows the tool's shaft and flute in the canvas during simulation.

A flute is the cutting edge of a tool. A shaft is the upper section of the tool and fits into a holder.

name: Bar Pull
tooltip: The bar pull strategy draws the stock from the main spindle. No toolpath is created with this strategy. The post is responsible for outputting the desired NC code.

name: Subspindle Grab
tooltip: The subspindle grab strategy extends the subspindle and grips the part in preparation for a stock transfer. No toolpath is created with this strategy. The post is responsible for outputting the desired NC code.

name: Subspindle Return
tooltip: The subspindle return strategy sends the subspindle back to the home position, for additional machining on the back of the part. No toolpath is created with this strategy. The post is responsible for outputting the desired NC code.

name: Tool Call
tooltip:
Calls a tool or empty station to pre-position it before subspindle moves, part-off, and transfer operations.

Use Tool Call to optimize tool selection, save time between operations, and reduce crash risk.

name: Turning Adaptive Roughing
tooltip:
Removes the bulk of the material from the part by cutting in both directions.

Use grooving tools with round inserts for this strategy.

name: Turning Chamfer
tooltip: Chamfers sharp corners that have not been chamfered in the design.

name: Turning Face
tooltip: Machines the front side of the part.

name: Turning Groove
tooltip: Enables roughing and finishing of the part using groove tools.

name: Turning Groove Finishing
tooltip:
Creates single or multiple finishing cuts to machine grooves.

Use this strategy on outside diameters, inside diameters, and face profiles.

name: Turning Groove Roughing
tooltip:
Removes the bulk of material from grooves by machining outside, inside and face grooves.

This strategy allows the tool to enter the groove either from the center or from the side. If the tool enters from the side, you can choose whether you want to remove material depth-first or width-first.

name: Turning Part
tooltip:
Cuts the part off from the bar.

Use this strategy before machining the part on another spindle or after the part has been fully machined.

name: Turning Profile
tooltip: The turning profile strategy is used for both Rough and Finish toolpaths. Roughing can be applied at any angle. Shown here as 3 separate Roughing Toolpaths.

name: Turning Profile Finishing
tooltip:
Finishes the part by machining outside diameters, inside diameters, and face profiles.

This strategy creates single or multiple cuts along the profile.

name: Turning Profile Roughing
tooltip:
Removes the bulk of the material from the part by machining outside diameters, inside diameters, and face profiles.

This strategy enables cutting vertically or horizontally.

name: Turning Single Groove
tooltip: The turning groove strategy is used for grooving at selected positions only. This can for instance be used to make a groove on the backside before threading.

name: Turning Thread
tooltip:
Makes cylindrical and conical threads.

Make sure that the CNC control has built-in support for synchronizing the spindle and feed.

name: Turning Trace
tooltip:
Creates a toolpath that traces a sketch profile.

Lets you machine challenging-to-reach areas of a part like undercuts or channels.

name: Automatic In-Process Stock Generation
tooltip:
Calculates a visual representation of the stock, known as in-process stock, which enables you to preview the effect that each toolpath has on the stock.

As you select a toolpath in the Browser, the in-process stock displays on the canvas. When you simulate a toolpath that has in-process stock calculated, the simulation begins with an accurate representation of the stock.

To turn the display of in-process stock on and off, use the Stock Visibility button in the Navigation bar at the bottom-center of the canvas.

name: Clear In-Process Stock Cache
tooltip:
Clears the stored in-process stock (IPS) meshes in all documents.

The cache stores IPS meshes for quicker generation. However, problems with IPS meshes can lead to documents closing unexpectedly. Clearing the cache can help prevent this, but it means that the IPS needs to be regenerated for all operations in all documents.

name: Edit Board Outline Sketch
tooltip:
Edits the primary sketch that defines the board outline.

Create a closed profile to define the board. You can project geometry from the assembly context to ensure the PCB outline stays updated with the mechanical assembly.

name: Layer Stack
tooltip:
Opens Design Preferences dialog.

Directly navigates to the Layer Stack page, making it easier to manage and adjust board layer composition.

name: Insert 2D PCB
tooltip: Inserts a previously saved 2D PCB in the canvas of the active 2D PCB.

name: Insert Design Block
tooltip:
Inserts a previously saved design block (.dbl) in the canvas of the active 2D PCB.

If a schematic is associated with the inserted design block a new sheet containing the schematic is added. Switch to the Schematic to view the sheet.

name: Insert Electronic Design
tooltip:
Inserts a previously saved project in the canvas of the active 2D PCB.

If a schematic is associated with the inserted project a new sheet containing the schematic is added. Switch to the Schematic to view the sheet.

name: Plated Hole (PTH)
tooltip:
Adds a plated hole to the 2D PCB.

Specify the drill parameter, indicating the hole diameter or slot length, then click to place a hole at a grid point.

name: Hide all Polygon Pour fills
tooltip:
Hide fill for all polygon pours.

Polygon pours are represented by an outline.

name: Polygon Pour
tooltip:
Create a polygon pour.

Polygons are used to create a copper sheet or layer for a signal, and must reside on a routing layer.

name: Re-fill Polygon Pours
tooltip:
Refill all polygon pours.

Doing this repairs any damage to polygon pours as a result of moving components or cutouts.

name: Restrict Area
tooltip:
Draw a restrict area polygon.

A restrict area prevents routing on the selected signal layers.

name: Show all Polygon Pour fills
tooltip:
Show fill for all polygon pours.

Restore the fills for polygon pours after they were hidden.

name: Autorouter
tooltip:
Starts the AutoRouter

If signal names are specified or signals are selected with the mouse, only these signals are routed. Without parameters the command will try to route all signals. The command has support for general rules and custom rules with net class scopes.

name: Fanout
tooltip:
Creates fanouts from devices and signals.

The command creates a routed wire and attached via from pads of the selected device or signal. Only surface mount devices (SMD) or ball-grid array (BGA) devices are fanned out; devices with through-hole pads are ignored.

name: QuickRoute Airwire
tooltip:
Automatically routes an individual airwire.

In QuickRoute Airwire mode, you select individual airwires to be automatically routed, and they are instantly routed according to design rules.

name: QuickRoute Guided
tooltip:
Automatically routes multiple signals along a sketched path.

Draw a selection line that intersects the signal objects you want to route concurrently (existing wires, pads, and vias). Right-click and draw the path for the selected signals. The signals are routed on the active layer with the fewest wire bends.

name: QuickRoute Multiple
tooltip:
Automatically routes multiple airwires simultaneously.

Draw a selection line that intersects the signal objects that you want to route concurrently (existing wires, pads, and vias). Continue to draw additional selection lines to add more signal objects. Right-click to route all the airwires connected to the selected objects. The signals are routed on the active layer.

name: QuickRoute Signal
tooltip:
Automatically routes a group of signal segments with the same name.

Select any signal object (airwire, wire, pad, or via) and the command instantly routes all airwires that are members of that signal.

name: QuickRoute Smooth
tooltip:
Automatically smooths the wire sequence on a selected signal.

QuickRoute Smooth reduces the number of wire bends and segments in the sequence.

name: QuickTune
tooltip: Automatically tunes the length of multiple traces, differential pairs, or busses by adding meanders.

name: Meander
tooltip: Length tunes the length of a single trace or differential pair by adding a meander.

name: Route Differential Pair
tooltip:
Converts unrouted connections of a differential pair into routed wires (tracks).

This command activates the differential-pair manual router, and the differential pairs in the design are highlighted. To begin routing a differential pair, click one of the highlighted differential pair airwire or copper objects.

name: Route Manual
tooltip:
Converts unrouted connections into routed wires (tracks).

This command activates the manual router, which converts airwires (unrouted connections) into real wires.

name: Route Multiple
tooltip:
Converts multiple unrouted connections into routed wires (tracks).

This command activates the manual router, which converts multiple airwires (unrouted connections) into real wires.

name: Via
tooltip:
Adds vias to a board.

When the Via command is active, a via symbol is attached to the cursor. Click to place a via at the current position.

name: Via Stitching
tooltip:
Adds Via Stitching to a board.

Adjust settings like offset, spacing, pattern, and via sizes. Click OK to apply Via Stitching. Draw a Polygon to target a specific area, if not covering the entire board.

name: Push to 3D PCB
tooltip:
Syncs changes from 2D PCB to 3D PCB. If no 3D PCB is linked, creates a new 3D PCB document. Provides preferences for object visibility and fidelity in the 3D PCB document.

Select the 2D PCB objects you want in the 3D PCB. Components without 3D models are identified and represented by rectangular shapes if you include them.

name: Unroute
tooltip:
Converts routed wires and vias into unrouted signals, and changes polygons to outlines.

Choose an unroute method to control which wires are affected.

name: Unroute All
tooltip: Converts all wire segments and vias to unrouted signals.

name: Unroute Incomplete
tooltip: Converts all stubs and incomplete segments to unrouted signals.

name: Hide All PCB Sketches
tooltip:
Hide All PCB Sketches

Conceals all visible PCB sketches.

name: Net Class and Signal Colors
tooltip: Displays custom net class and signal colors to make them easier to differentiate. Press Shift+A to show or hide colors in the canvas. Customize appearance in the Inspector or Properties panel.

name: Show All PCB Sketches
tooltip:
Show All PCB Sketches

Makes all hidden PCB sketches visible.

name: Bottom Origins
tooltip: Show or hide component origin markers on the bottom layer.
where: PCB Editor > DESIGN > VIEW > PCB Origins
paths: PCB Editor > DESIGN > VIEW > PCB Origins
PCB Editor > DOCUMENT > VIEW > PCB Origins
PCB Editor > Rules > VIEW > PCB Origins
PCB Editor > Manufacturing > VIEW > PCB Origins
PCB Editor > SIMULATION > VIEW > PCB Origins
PCB Editor > UTILITIES > VIEW > PCB Origins

name: Top Origins
tooltip: Show or hide component origin markers on the top layer.
where: PCB Editor > DESIGN > VIEW > PCB Origins
paths: PCB Editor > DESIGN > VIEW > PCB Origins
PCB Editor > DOCUMENT > VIEW > PCB Origins
PCB Editor > Rules > VIEW > PCB Origins
PCB Editor > Manufacturing > VIEW > PCB Origins
PCB Editor > SIMULATION > VIEW > PCB Origins
PCB Editor > UTILITIES > VIEW > PCB Origins

name: Mark Local Origin
tooltip:
Defines a mark on the drawing area.

The X and Y coordinates of the mouse cursor relative to that point are displayed above the canvas, with an R prefix, polar coordinates with P prefix. This command is useful when defining locations of components or cutouts. Enter MARK; to turn the mark off.

name: Export Gerber, NC Drill, Assembly and Drawing Outputs
tooltip:
Generate Gerber, NC Drill, Assembly and Drawing outputs and save the ZIP output file in current directory.

The outputs generation will use the best matching CAMJOB template based on the design's number of signal (copper) layers.

name: Export ODB++ Output
tooltip:
Generate ODB++ output and save it to the specified compressed output file (default = ZIP).

The ODB++ output generation will use any valid CAMJOB file that includes ODB++ output configuration and resides in the ODB++ output directory. If there is no such CAMJOB file in the output directory the best matching CAMJOB template based on the design's number of copper layers will be used instead.

name: Design Preferences
tooltip:
Edits parameters that drive design geometry.

Preferences include Layer Stack, Annular Ring, Pad/SMD Shapes, Thermal Isolation, and Masks. Adjusting these settings automatically calculates PCB geometries according to preferences.

name: Check Design Rules
tooltip:
Checks design rules.

Errors, if detected, are displayed in the Errors panel. Real-time rule checking can be enabled in the application settings for instant error detection.

name: Design Rules
tooltip:
Creates and edits design rules.

Design rules are evaluated each time rules are checked. Can load design rule presets from external sources and scope design rules to defined parameters.

name: Analyze Signal
tooltip:
Calculates signal integrity for a selected signal. Returns impedance, propagation delay and other values for each segment of the signal path in tabular and graphical form.

Define the frequency and target impedance range to flag and identify impedance issues to resolve in the circuit design.

name: Export PCB Data for Ansys
tooltip:
Exports PCB data to Ansys Electronics Desktop.

Specify the exported file location and the file type. Hand the file off to the Ansys Electronics Desktop.

name: Capture Image...
tooltip:
Captures the current canvas as an image.

Set the image size and resolution then set the file type (*.png, *.jpg, *.tiff) and file name.

name: Render
tooltip:
Creates a high-quality rendered image of your scene using cloud or local background rendering technology.

Choose the desired image size, settings, cloud or local render, and click Render to start the rendering process. Finished renderings will appear in your Rendering Gallery.

name: Light
tooltip:
Adds light to control illumination, shadows, and highlights in your render.

Combine scene lights with environment lighting in Scene Settings for realistic results. You can add up to eight lights per design.

name: Scene Settings
tooltip: Set the environment and lighting for the scene. This setting only affects the Rendering workspace.

name: Texture Map Controls
tooltip:
Sets the orientation of the texture applied to the body or component.

Select the object to modify then the Projection Type and the Axis. Modify the Mapping Transform using the manipulator or fields in the dialog.

name: Add Bus
tooltip:
Draws buses on the bus layer of a schematic.

A Bus is a collection of nets. A Bus has a specification and is drawn as one or more bus line segments. The bus specification can include a unique alias, which is a short name used to identify the bus.

name: Break Out Bus
tooltip:
Breaks out a single, selected, or all nets as new wires extending from a bus.

Automatically add wires with net labels extending from a bus, saving time, and reducing errors.

name: Break Out Pins
tooltip:
Breaks out all or a selection of pins from the part by extending nets a short distance from the pins.

New nets connected to pins are drawn and can be automatically named and labeled.

name: Junction
tooltip:
Places a dot at intersecting nets.

A connection dot is placed at the intersection of nets to be connected. Junctions can be placed only on nets. If placed on the intersection of different nets, the user is given the option to connect the nets.

name: Label
tooltip:
Attaches text labels to buses and nets.
